what_this_is: The index-calculus baseline ledger (the ratchet). For each curve and size, the current best verified IC pipeline with its protocol, receipts and end-to-end S, and its distance to the matched rho and to Bernstein-Lange. One row, one experiment: no row combines numbers from two experiments. Human view: BASELINES.md.
rule: AGENTS.md, 'Success criterion: iterative improvement of the index-calculus baseline' (owner, 2026-10-15; cryptanalysis#919, crypto#1908). Every verified, measured improvement over a baseline row is a success; a landed improvement replaces the row and the old row moves to ratchet_history with its delta. The gap to rho is the distance remaining, not a gate.

conventions.gap_direction: Every gap is IC cost over the reference's cost, so a value above 1 is the distance still to close and a value below 1 means the IC is cheaper on that boundary. The sources' own 'online speedup' (rho over IC) is the reciprocal; it is kept in each row's source_figure.
conventions.S: S = cost / sqrt(r) in the unit named on the row. The unit differs between experiments (a batched affine addition in crypto's ic price; a rho step of the run's tuned rho at n=83; a rho group operation of CPU at n=19). S values compare inside a row only; the gap ratios carry no unit.
conventions.cold: Every phase for one fresh target with empty caches: reusable setup (factor base, relations, linear algebra / log table, index) plus the online interval. A row whose experiment did not charge a phase names it (n=83: uncharged_phases, factor-base construction); such a cold S is a lower bound and its ratios are not every-phase figures. A row measured in wall time on one host says so (n=83: headline_scope).
conventions.online: From the first target-dependent operation to the verified scalar, reusable setup excluded (AGENTS.md, 'The default IC objective is one target').
conventions.setup: s_ic_setup = s_ic_cold - s_ic_online on every row that carries it: the reusable work for the first target that the row's experiment charged, the relation-collection / rank stage and the linear algebra (or the verified load of its cached factor-log table) included, less every phase the row names in uncharged_phases. It is all reusable work only on a row without uncharged_phases: n=41, 53 and 61 (crypto rule v3, whose setup includes factor-base selection and build, relation collection, linear algebra and the descent's solver). Both n=83 rows exclude factor-base construction (each process loads the K600 base from a file); B's n=83 row (other_records) also excludes its linear algebra (51.3 ms) and setup input control (32.3 ms). n=19 carries no s_ic_setup. It never means setup without the rank stage. Where an experiment times the rank stage separately (n=83), the row may also split s_ic_setup into s_ic_rank_stage + s_ic_setup_without_rank_stage, in the row's own unit; the split is optional, s_ic_setup is not. Corrected 2026-10-16, see corrections.
conventions.intervals: 95% bootstrap over targets unless the row says otherwise. Inverting a ratio of means inverts its interval endpoints exactly.
conventions.evidence_tiers: Tier 0 / Tier 1 as in AGENTS.md 'CPU performance evidence tiers'. 'crypto isolated_bench container' means one cloud container through crypto's isolation tool (pinned CPU, PSI gate, contended runs re-run), without a provider allocation receipt: it is neither Tier 0 nor Tier 1 here. 'exploratory' has no pinned CPU or allocation receipt.
conventions.tuned_rho: 'Tuned rho' means A's tuned StrongRhoG worker rT770 (Fold field kernel, 64 lanes, DP 6, escape off; crypto 770f6a69 examples/n83_rho_optimization_eval.rs with research/n83_evaluation_20261012/optimization/selected_config.json), the fastest correct n=83 reference found by experiments/koblitz-n83-reconcile-20261014. It has been run at n=83 only. ParallelRho (crypto ic price) is crypto's own 'tuned signed-Frobenius walk' (64 lanes in lockstep); it is reported where it is the matched rho, and it is not rT770.

baselines.s_ic_setup_derivation: result.json (run 38862448935): rho_ms_per_step 3.16660e-4 ms x sqrt(r) = 29,314.2 ms per unit; rank stage mean(kS rank_stage_ms) 257,814.27 ms = 8.79486 -> 8.7949; setup mean_setup_ms.cS 25,575.25 ms = 0.87245 -> 0.8725 (cached-table load and verification included); s_ic_setup = 8.79486 + 0.87245 = 9.66731 -> 9.6673 = s_ic_cold 9.68045 - s_ic_online 0.013137. Every S here is rounded once from the unrounded quotient, so rounded parts need not add up (8.7949 + 0.8725 = 9.6674, while the unrounded sum rounds to 9.6673). s_ic_rank_stage read 8.7948 until 2026-10-17 (a rounding slip, corrections); S_cold_without_rank.cS 0.8856 is setup without the rank stage plus online. This row first landed with s_ic_setup 0.8856, setup without the rank stage plus online, which is not the field's meaning (see corrections).

rank_stage_probes.note: totals over the two rank processes (1,200 attempts per arm); mean per attempt 2,480,244.6 vs 1,678,902.8; deterministic in the rank seed

operation_counts.rank_stage_wall_decomposition: rank-stage wall ratio 3.3737 = 1.4773 (fewer probes; a count, deterministic in the rank seed) x 2.2837 (per-probe wall time: wall ns per probe 584.48 vs 255.94, measured on this one host). The 2.2837 is not a host-speed factor: a kP probe (full canonicalization, base table, sequential) and a kS probe (lift_scan, compact table, prefetch loop) are not the same work, so it mixes cheaper per-probe work with host and memory-system effects; until field operations per probe are emitted it cannot be split into the two.
operation_counts.not_counted: setup and index build emit no operation count comparable to probes, so no single end-to-end operation-count ratio exists; the rank stage is 94.6% (pP) and 90.9% (stack) of end-to-end cold wall time

uncharged_phases.factor_base_construction: Not charged to either arm. Every IC process loads the K600 base (99,600 points) from base_n83_K600.jsonl (base_source retained_header; base_load about 0.31 s is parsing only); its construction (scan x from 1, lift, cofactor projection, first 600 signed-Frobenius orbits) was not timed. conventions.cold lists the factor base, and AGENTS.md says a missing phase makes the total unknown, not zero. The omission is common to both arms, so R > 1 holds for any construction cost X >= 0, but R falls with X and the cold S rises: R 3.2312 / S 9.7146 at X = 1 s, 3.1629 / 10.0216 at 10 s, 2.8483 / 11.7272 at 60 s. So 3.2391 is an upper bound on the every-phase ratio and S 9.6805 a lower bound on the every-phase cold S. B's README disclosed the same exclusion; this row did not until 2026-10-16. Measured 2026-10-17 (measurement_status): X = 427.524 ms, so the bounds are tight: R 3.2357 and cold S 9.6950 at that X (illustrative, mixes hosts).
uncharged_phases.linear_algebra: represented by the verified load of the cached factor-log table (89.6 ms in cP and cS, against 90.5-90.7 ms of measured LA in every rank process)
uncharged_phases.measurement_status: Measured 2026-10-17 in the preregistered replay (https://github.com/aburan28/cryptanalysis/actions/runs/39007026856, INTEL(R) XEON(R) PLATINUM 8573C): one cold in-process construction construct:83:1:600 (base_source constructed_in_process_x_scan, base_scanned_x 1266, base hash d4a4da26...a9f7 equal to the retained file's) took X = timing_ms.base_load 427.524 ms, 65.541 ms more than the retained-file load on the same host (361.984 ms). With this row's unit (29,314.2 ms) and X added to both arms' E2E: R 3.2357 (was 3.2391), cold S 9.6950 (was 9.6805), gap to the tuned rho 94.56 (was 94.42). These every-phase figures are illustrative: they add an Intel-host X to EPYC-host wall times (protocol: any R(X) built this way mixes two hosts); the row's R and S are unchanged. X is about 0.15% of the stack's end-to-end cold wall time (283.8 s); R falls below 2 only at X >= 351.6 s. The section 5a band stays uncomputable (open).

baselines.section_5a_band: Not computable from this run. The IC arms emit rank-stage probes and root calls, online probes and stored states, but no group additions, scalar multiplications, canonicalizations, fold rotations or index inserts, so the unpriced native work cannot be priced at 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE per operation and the IC / rho gap (94.4) has no band. The gap holds as a wall-time figure on this one host only. Follow-up (README, 'Follow-up'): emit counted group operations from the IC producer in a new experiment; the frozen producer is not changed.
baselines.replication: Replayed on another host class, 2026-10-17: exact determinism pass (replay_pass). The preregistered K1 replay (cryptanalysis:experiments/koblitz-n83-replay-20261017/PROTOCOL.md, frozen at commit 863f6090; workflow n83-replay.yml at d1c361e3) ran as https://github.com/aburan28/cryptanalysis/actions/runs/39007026856 (job 117321470019) on INTEL(R) XEON(R) PLATINUM 8573C, not the original AMD EPYC 9V74, so another_host_class is true by the frozen rule (same runner image, kernel and toolchain; same binary sha256). Order kS, kP, kP, kS, rank seed 101, full rank: all six runs valid; every per-attempt probe count (first 100 and all 600) and the relation digest equal the archived K1 records (serials 42, 43); the constructed K600 base hash equals the retained one. Reported, not gated: per-probe wall ratio kP / kS 2.6583 on the Intel host (first 100 attempts 2.7013) against 2.2905 for K1 (2.2837 both blocks) on the EPYC, so the 3.2391 wall-time headline and every S on this row are host-dependent; the operation-count ratio 1.4773 is not. The replay did not re-measure the cold arms, so no new R or S. One replay, one other host class, two processes per arm, no interval. Archived at cryptanalysis:experiments/koblitz-n83-replay-20261017/RESULTS.md (artifact n83-replay-39007026856-1, zip sha256 b8226c794d7a3c5c7ab369487399f25869bff3661ca17c521c2c2da0b8fb951d). Preregistration of the original run is provable from GitHub records (protocol commit 24abca74 is the parent of the result commit on branch claude/n83-stacked), not from main's squashed history; sheriff cases SHF-20261016-3caa6f R1, SHF-20261017-e4d7f6 R1-R.
baselines.next_improvement: The rank stage is 257.8 s of the 283.8 s end-to-end cold cost (91%): cut it (fewer or cheaper attempts; the guided minimum-rank policy), then setup (lift_scan in the index build, cSI, is 1.33x faster cold without rank). Gap to the tuned rho is still 94x; the BL arm has not been re-run on the stack.
